study.scope: Add 503 identity-selected observed Train histories to 542 existing histories. Keep all 537 Train family identifiers, every original input/label and every Dev/Test source unchanged. Existing same-seed controls use identical GRU, initialization, losses, cross-fit family assignments, optimizer, batch size and maximum epoch budgets. More rows mean more updates and runtime; report both. Do not use the rejected mean-difference selector.
observationAssumptions: Daily positive allocation follows a symmetric Dirichlet; fit its integer concentration separately inside every fitting source partition.
Daily stockouts are modeled as noninformative right censoring. Complete periods are selected by inventory availability; their coverage and order loss do not identify all latent demand.
selection: Report seeds 42,43,44; candidate seed stays 42. No Test or frozen 27-source holdout evaluation or tuning.
Reuse the accepted demand-selection-v2 adoption criteria before observing candidate Dev results: seed 42 must lower complete weekly CRPS and each order-loss ratio 1,3,9 against the retained GRU.
Seed 42 daily CRPS may increase by at most 10 percent; complete weekly 80-percent coverage may not decrease, and daily observation NLL and weekly daily-allocation NLL must not increase.

At least two of three seeds must improve weekly CRPS, mean order loss and daily-allocation NLL against their same-seed retained controls. Also report all comparisons with the currently retained seed-42 model.

Only after these gates pass, replace the demand weights in a candidate with the frozen language constructor and manager policy. Require lower actual retail total loss, preserved parameter/evidence accuracy and needed-request recovery, and no increase in invalid handoffs or unnecessary requests before promotion.
Do not claim the legacy generated Test target or real organizational effectiveness from a demand-only Dev comparison.
